problem_statement: The paper frames the task as generating synthetic financial market data from a real-world dataset of correlated currency pairs, so that a model can learn the joint distribution of the data. It treats this as a generative modelling problem in finance, with the goal of matching the data distribution as closely as possible.
problem_statement_quotes: We use a real world financial dataset consisting 0f correlated currency pairs and compare twO models in their ability to learn the resulting distribution
classical_baseline: The classical baseline is a restricted Boltzmann machine, which the paper describes as a completely classical model for the same generative task. The paper compares it against a quantum circuit Born machine under matched parameter counts and similar constraints.
classical_baseline_quotes: As a benchmark of fairness, WC fixed the models to have the same numbers of trainable parameters and found that the simulated Born machine always performed at least a5 well a5 the RBM
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper is a finance application comparing generative models.
